captions.title: The built turret, from every side
captions.text: The assembly built in the first half of the video, now simulated: the camera circles the pan-tilt stack. Four drones are about to fly their seeded swarm program.

captions.title: Track, pick, aim, wait for the operator
captions.text: The turret camera (picture-in-picture) finds the drones, tracks them across frames and picks a target. A pellet is a point mass with quadratic air drag, gravity and the wind the turret estimates from its mast anemometer, so the aim point leads the drone.

captions.title: Hit: slow motion
captions.text: drone3 takes a pellet. Slowed 4x, the camera close on the drone. The kernel reports which body the pellet struck; a scenario rule maps that to damage, with no dice roll.

captions.title: Next target (2x speed), camera circling the swarm
captions.text: The operator authorizes one track at a time. Misses are real: drag and gravity drop the pellet, wind pushes it sideways.

captions.title: Closing on drone4
captions.text: Pellets pass within centimetres of drone4 before one lands.

captions.title: Hit: slow motion
captions.text: drone4 is hit (slowed 4x). Functional damage, then the physics does the rest: it ends tilted past 80 degrees or falls.

captions.title: Back to the swarm (2x speed)
captions.text: Remaining drones keep flying their program; the turret re-acquires.

captions.title: The rest of the 60 s run (4x speed)
captions.text: Pellet drag, gravity and wind decide the outcome; the final counters are on the end card.

captions.title: Last seconds, real time: back around the turret
captions.text: The same turret at the end of the run, the camera circling it again.
